2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner.

3. The present application has been filed at the instance of the informant-victim under Section 378(3) of the Cr.P.C. seeking leave to prefer an appeal against the judgment of acquittal dated 12.04.2010 passed in C.T. (Sessions) No.53 of 2007 by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate-cum-Assistant sessions Judge, Dhenkanal thereby acquitting the accused-Opposite Parties of the charges under Sections 376 of the I.P.C.

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate-cum-Assistant sessions Judge, Dhenkanal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On perusal of the record it appears that no leave application has been filed at the instance of the State seeking leave to prefer a government appeal.

4. On a careful consideration of the factual background of the present case this Court observed that the Petitioner who was the victim-informant before the trial court, being aggrieved by the judgment of acquittal of the learned trial court dated 12.04.2010, has approached this Court by filing this application seeking leave to prefer an appeal.
It is not disputed that the Petitioner is a victim and she was informant to the present case.
Moreover, the allegation made in the F.I.R. was heinous in nature i.e. involving the offence under Section 376 of the I.P.C.
So far as Section 372 of the Cr.P.C. is concerned, it was amended in the year 2009 and the amendment came into effect on 31.12.2009 by Kabita Parida vs Bijaya Behera .....

Amendment Act 5 of 2009 by introducing a new proviso to the said section.

The newly added proviso provides for a right to the victim to prefer an appeal against any order of acquittal and such appeal shall lie to the Court to which an appeal could ordinarily lie against an order of conviction of such Court.

Since against the judgment of acquittal in the present case an appeal would have lied to this Court had the accused been convicted, there is no dispute with regard to the proposition that the appeal would lie to this Court in view of the specific provision contained in the proviso to Section 372 of the Cr.P.C. conferring a right on the victim to prefer an appeal directly to this Court.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that no leave is required under Section 378 Cr.P.C. to prefer an appeal by the victim.

5. In view of the aforesaid legal position Registry is directed to convert the present application to that of a criminal appeal and that the matter be placed before the appropriate assigned bench expeditiously.
( Aditya Kumar Mohapatra)
